decisions.summary: Narrowed the publish_log card-number check so it stops withholding entries that merely contain a long identifier.
decisions.rationale: The card pattern matches any 13-19 digit run, and Jules session ids are 19 digits, so three consecutive decisions were withheld from the public operations log for mentioning a session id. That log is a graded deliverable and the withholding was silent, because failing closed is the design and nobody was reading the exit code. The check now requires the Luhn checksum AND a major-industry-identifier of 3-6, which every payment card issued by Visa, Mastercard, Amex or Discover has and which arbitrary numeric identifiers do not. Luhn alone was insufficient: the session id in question passes it. This narrows precision, not coverage.

open_questions.question: Future improvement, not urgent: switch GitHub Pages from legacy branch-deploy to a GitHub Actions build-and-deploy workflow. Today the ops loop commits rendered docs/ to main every cycle, which is what let a long-lived feature branch collide with generated output. With an Actions deploy the site is uploaded as an artifact, so docs/ need never be committed at all. The catch: the site is rendered from ledger.db, which lives only on the lab box, so the workflow would have to regenerate it from the committed reports/ledger-dump.json instead — publish_log.py currently reads sqlite, not the JSON dump. Deferred 2026-08-07: the legacy build is healthy (7 of last 7 runs green, site current) and the deadline is the binding constraint. Operator's idea.

app/main.py hardcodes its Gemini model as a default rather than reading models.work from invariants.toml, which AGENTS.md #5 requires. The default was gemini-2.5-flash, which returns 404 'no longer available to new users', so the deployed service answered every permitted question with an error while the refusal path kept working — a failure invisible to anyone who only tested a refusal. Worked around on 2026-08-07 by setting UNDRA_APP_MODEL on the Cloud Run service and pinning it in cloudbuild.yaml. The proper fix is for the app to read the model from configuration, so a model retirement is a config change rather than a silent outage.
open_questions.answer: Worked around 2026-08-07 and verified: UNDRA_APP_MODEL=gemini-3.6-flash is set on the Cloud Run service and pinned in cloudbuild.yaml, and the deployed app now answers permitted questions from the model. The question stays worth acting on — the model is pinned in two places rather than read from invariants.toml — but it no longer blocks anything.
